decisions.reason: Although it uses the firm's glass-wafer and structuring know-how, glass-silicon wafers with vertical through contacts require more distant integration and interconnect capabilities, and without evidence of becoming a strategic focus management would likely reallocate resources.

Carrier wafers are very close to the firm's existing substrate and thin-wafer handling capabilities and fit its stated direction toward reusable carriers, so the firm can readily learn from customers and improve them.

The copper interposer glass wafer stretches the firm's capabilities but still builds on its core glass, coating and precision-processing knowledge, and as a flagship semiconductor-packaging product it is likely to be retained for further development.
An off-the-shelf glass and quartz wafer line is squarely within the firm's established knowledge base and directly broadens its core offer, making discontinuation unlikely.

Glass-based circuit boards are the furthest from the firm's narrow established wafer-substrate specialization, so under an absorptive-capacity logic management would be prone to exit if early market learning did not quickly validate the concept.
